cards.text: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to the saints at Philippi (Philippians 1:1). He's sending Epaphroditus back to them and tells them to welcome him with great joy (Philippians 2:25, 29). Now Paul writes, "Finally, my brothers…" and turns to what's next.

cards.question: Paul calls them his brothers. What does he tell them to do in the Lord?

cards.text: Then Paul says he's writing them the same things again. Friend, I'm the same way. I've told my oven "Don't you DARE burn this batch" every single morning since I got here.

cards.question: Paul says writing the same things to the Philippians again is a lot of trouble for him.
Paul says writing the same things again is no trouble for him. What does he say it is for the Philippians?

cards.text: Then Paul's tone flips HARD: "Watch out for those dogs, those workers of evil, those mutilators of the flesh!" Rejoice one second, RED ALERT the next, like a smoke alarm going off in the middle of a birthday batch.
Then Paul says, "it is we who are the circumcision…" and he describes that group. First off, they worship by the Spirit of God.

cards.question: Paul says it is "we" who are the circumcision, Paul included, and they worship by the Spirit of God. Who does Paul say they glory in?
Paul says the "we" who are the circumcision, Paul included, put great confidence in the flesh.

cards.text: Then Paul says he could have that kind of confidence in the flesh himself. Friend, if I listed MY credentials, it'd be one line: found at the bottom of a bakery bin, priced at 25 cents.

cards.question: Paul says he could have confidence in the flesh himself. If anyone else thinks he has grounds for that confidence, how much does Paul say he has?

cards.text: Then Paul lists it all: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, and as to the law, a Pharisee.
As to zeal, Paul says he was persecuting the church. Friend, that one's heavy, and he puts it right there on the list.

cards.question: As to righteousness in the law, Paul says he was faultless.

cards.text: After that whole list, Paul writes one little word: "But."

cards.question: Paul says whatever was gain to him, he now counts as loss for the sake of Christ.

cards.text: And Paul goes BIGGER, friend. Not just that list, but ALL things he counts as loss, and he says he has lost all things for Christ.

cards.question: Paul counts all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of what?
How does Paul say he considers all the things he lost?

cards.text: RUBBISH. Paul takes the most stacked résumé in the room and treats it like an old takeout menu from the junk drawer I used to live in, all so he may gain Christ and be found in Him.

cards.question: Paul doesn't want his own righteousness from the ___. He wants the righteousness from God that comes through ___ in Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul says what he wants now, and it's NOT his old title back. He wants to know Christ and the power of His resurrection.

cards.question: Paul says he wants the power of Christ's resurrection but not the fellowship of His sufferings.
Paul wants to know Christ, even sharing in His sufferings and being conformed to Him in His death. What does Paul want to attain?

cards.text: Notice the little word Paul tucks in there: somehow. I'll be honest, friend, that little word is gonna stick with me for a while.
